name: Cloudflare R2
summary: S3-compatible object storage from Cloudflare that charges nothing for data going out.
intro: R2 is object storage that answers the S3 API at an account endpoint, `https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`, with the region set to `auto`. Existing S3 SDKs and tools work after changing the endpoint and keys. Cloudflare Workers can also read and write buckets directly through a binding, without signing requests.

What sets it apart is billing. Reading data out of R2 costs nothing in egress. You pay for storage ($0.015 per GB-month in the Standard class) and for operations ($4.50 per million writes, $0.36 per million reads). That makes it popular for public downloads, media and datasets read from other clouds. An Infrequent Access class costs $0.01 per GB-month but adds a retrieval fee and a 30-day minimum. Basin Catalog (formerly R2 Data Catalog) can run a managed Apache Iceberg REST catalog inside a bucket; it became generally available on 1 October 2026.
strengths: No egress fees, so serving or copying data out is not billed per GB
S3 API compatibility: point existing SDKs and tools at a new endpoint
Built-in bindings for Cloudflare Workers, plus public buckets on custom domains
Free tier of 10 GB-month storage, 1 million writes and 10 million reads each month
limits: Only part of the S3 API: no object versioning, bucket policies, object tagging or ACLs
Each key can be written about once per second; faster writes get HTTP 429
Far fewer storage classes and lifecycle options than S3, and no archive tier
Infrequent Access charges a retrieval fee and bills at least 30 days

worksWith.how: can host a managed catalog for

snippet.title: Create a bucket with Wrangler, then use the aws CLI against R2
source: npx wrangler r2 bucket create acme-media
# any S3 tool works against the account endpoint; the region is "auto"
aws s3 cp video.mp4 s3://acme-media/videos/video.mp4 --endpoint-url "$R2" --region auto

story: By 2021 egress, the per-GB fee for data leaving a cloud, was often the largest line on an object storage bill. In July 2021 Cloudflare’s Matthew Prince and Nitin Rao published “AWS’s Egregious Egress”, arguing that wholesale bandwidth prices had fallen 93% over a decade while AWS’s egress fees had fallen only 25%, and that the fees helped lock customers in.

Two months later, on 28 September 2021, Cloudflare announced R2: object storage with full S3 API compatibility and no egress fees, building on its Bandwidth Alliance commitment, at $0.015 per GB-month. Greg McKeon’s announcement called egress fees “just a tax developers have grown accustomed to paying”. R2 entered open beta in May 2022 and became generally available on 21 September 2022, by which point more than 12,000 developers had joined the beta and Cloudflare Images was running on it in production.

The pitch is multi-cloud: keep one copy of the data in R2 and read it from any cloud, or serve it to the public, without paying per GB. Cloudflare has since built analytics on top, starting with a managed Apache Iceberg catalog inside buckets.

choices.why: Cloudflare argued egress was priced far above what bandwidth really costs. R2 bills for storage and operations instead ($4.50 per million writes, $0.36 per million reads), so reading data out costs nothing per GB.

choices.choice: The S3 API instead of a new one
choices.why: Existing SDKs and tools work as built, and customers can start serving objects from R2 while they are still migrating them from another cloud.
Buckets bind directly to Cloudflare Workers, so code running on Cloudflare’s network can read and write objects without signing requests.

timeline.text: Cloudflare attacks AWS egress pricing in July and announces R2 on 28 September
Open beta in May; generally available on 21 September
R2 Data Catalog: a managed Iceberg catalog in a bucket, in public beta (April)
The catalog, renamed Basin Catalog, becomes generally available on 1 October
